gen-dafont-arkhip-poppins: Poppins stands tall and sturdy, its curves loose and never knotted at the ends, a plain sans with no stroke flicker. Arkhip, though, floats its geometric letters well apart, with a c open like a bent paperclip, so a long page feels spacious.
gen-dafont-aurulent-sans-fs-erode: Dignified from the first line, with outward-pointing tips up top. Erode's text serif has a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb of stroke weight, which gives the pair a settled, editorial grace.
gen-dafont-aurulent-sans-fs-karma: Aurulent Sans points its terminal tips outward in an organic, friendly way, while Karma keeps its classic serif close to cap height. One is loose and natural; the other is steady and trustworthy.
gen-dafont-aurulent-sans-fs-recia: Sharp, authoritative Recia is the body here, under Aurulent Sans. Its light modulation shows mainly up close, and its openings stay generous, so a long stretch of text moves along without snagging the eye.
gen-dafont-berylium-fs-neco: Berylium draws smooth, tube-like lines, with g and s curling wide and letters keeping a polite distance. Neco's best quality is its reed-pen swell from hairline to stem, which gives the serif body a dignified, open feel.
gen-dafont-berylium-fs-recia: Minimal and contemporary, Berylium traces every glyph with a single thickness and a pen-plotter smoothness. Recia, the serif body, adds a subtle gradient of weight along each curve, and that quiet shift is the pair's real strength.
gen-dafont-biko-fs-erode: Biko enters each curved letter with a big visible lead-in, and its strokes never vary in thickness, so it feels cozy and blunt. Erode's text serif, with a light touch of modulation, reads in a tall, dignified rhythm.
gen-dafont-biko-fs-merriweather-sans: Rounded-rod strokes of one weight and a big visible entrance into every curve make Biko feel cozy. Merriweather Sans follows with tall, sturdy lowercase and an e that opens clearly, so longer lines read large and steady.
gen-dafont-biko-fs-neco: Biko draws every curve without stress, in one cozy, clean weight. Neco brings a classic serif with lightly thinned links in the g and sturdy bowls, and that measured swell is what makes the pairing distinctive.
gen-dafont-biko-fs-recia: Cozy and clean, Biko holds a constant pen pressure through every curve and its big entrance strokes. Recia takes over below with a low-to-medium contrast serif, sharp and authoritative, so the page moves from soft to crisp.
